cases.reason: Both meet every criterion, but Y hands over a ready-to-print adapted worksheet with timed steps, evidence grid and PEEL boxes, so there is less to make tonight.
Both rewrites are accurate and pitched well, but X adds headings, a glossary, comprehension questions and a clear note of what changed, while Y gives the text alone.

Y is an actual one-page student sheet with code-matched fix tasks and a labelled model paragraph, whereas X is a lesson plan the teacher still has to turn into a handout; both have a small literature slip (X puts a paraphrase in quotation marks, Y says 'his own' is repeated when it appears once).
X fits a 20-minute slot with accurate French, a checked answer key and a parent role that only means listening and signing, while Y runs to 30-35 minutes and asks more of parents.
